message.content:
Build "Login with Google" (Google OAuth) into the Nxeon customer portal at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router; custom auth using `jose` JWT session cookies + `bcryptjs`, NOT NextAuth). The Google OAuth credentials are provided by the operator as env vars `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (already the agreed names). The redirect/callback URL is `${APP_URL}/api/auth/google/callback` where `APP_URL` is an existing env var (currently https://nxeon.cloud). Verify with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate` then `npx tsc --noEmit` (exit 0) and `npx tsx --test test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` (stay green). Do NOT run `prisma db push`, build, deploy, or commit — I will. Report files changed + the new schema field.

## Read first (match existing patterns exactly)
- `lib/auth.ts` and `lib/api-auth.ts` — how a normal login issues the session (jose sign, the cookie NAME, options, expiry, and any `createSession`/`setSessionCookie` helper). REUSE that exact session-issuance for the Google path — do not invent a new session scheme.
- `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts` — the existing OAuth pattern (state/PKCE, token exchange via fetch) to model the Google flow on.
- The login page + form (grep for the password login form / the `signIn`/login server action, likely under `app/(auth)/login` or `app/login`).
- `User` model in prisma/schema.prisma, and how a User is created at signup (fields required: passwordHash, etc.) so a Google-created user is valid.

## Schema (additive, nullable → safe for db push)
Add to `User`: `googleId String? @unique` (and `avatarUrl String?` if the model has no avatar field and you want to store the Google picture — optional). Run `npx prisma generate` after (NOT db push).

## The flow
1. **Start route** `app/api/auth/google/route.ts` (GET): generate a random `state` (CSRF), store it in a short-lived httpOnly cookie, and 302-redirect to Google's authorize URL (`https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`) with `client_id=GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `redirect_uri=${APP_URL}/api/auth/google/callback`, `response_type=code`, `scope=openid email profile`, `state`, `access_type=online`, `prompt=select_account`.
2. **Callback** `app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts` (GET): 
   - Verify `state` matches the cookie (reject on mismatch — CSRF).
   - Exchange `code` at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` (POST form: code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code) via fetch.
   - Fetch the profile from `https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo` (Bearer access_token) OR decode the id_token — get `sub` (Google user id), `email`, `email_verified`, `name`, `picture`. Require `email_verified` true; reject otherwise.
   - **Find or link the user**: by `googleId` first; else by `email` (link `googleId` onto the existing account — this lets an existing password user sign in with Google); else CREATE a new User (email, name, `googleId`, a null/placeholder passwordHash consistent with how the schema allows password-less users — check whether passwordHash is nullable; if it's required, generate a random unusable hash so the account can't be password-logged-in until they set one). Respect any required User fields/defaults used at normal signup.
   - Issue the SAME session cookie a normal login issues (reuse the helper from lib/auth.ts), then 302-redirect to the dashboard (e.g. `/dashboard`).
   - On any error, redirect to the login page with an error query param the login page can show.
3. **Login page UI**: add a "Continue with Google" button (styled to the Nxeon dark theme, with a Google glyph/text) that links to `/api/auth/google`. Place it under the existing email/password form with an "or" divider. If `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is unset, HIDE the button (so it doesn't show a broken flow before the operator adds creds) — check the env server-side and pass a boolean to the client component.

## Security + correctness
- httpOnly + secure + sameSite=lax cookies for state; short TTL.
- Never log the client secret or tokens. Read creds from `process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` at request time (not module top-level, so an unset value doesn't crash boot).
- Preserve every existing auth guard/test; the callback is a route handler (not a "use server" action) so the guard test is unaffected, but double-check you didn't add an unguarded server action.
- Handle Google's "app in testing" mode gracefully (a non-test user gets Google's own error screen before reaching us — nothing to do, but the callback must handle `error` query param from Google by redirecting to login with a friendly message).

Finish only when `prisma generate` + `tsc --noEmit` are clean and the guard test passes. Report: the new User field(s), the two route files, the session-issuance helper you reused, and the login-page change.

## Summary

Built "Login with Google" into the Nxeon portal using the existing custom `jose`/`bcryptjs` auth (no NextAuth), reusing the exact session-issuance path.

### New User schema field(s)
In `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma`, added to `User`:
- `googleId String? @unique` — the Google `sub`; NULL for password-only accounts. Additive + nullable, so `db push` is safe.
- `avatarUrl String?` — optional Google profile picture (the model had no avatar field).

### Files changed
- `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma` — the two fields above.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/google-oauth.ts` (new) — OAuth helper modeled on `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts`: endpoint constants, `googleOauthConfigured()` (reads creds at request time, never module top-level), `googleRedirectUri()` (`${APP_URL}/api/auth/google/callback`), `googleAuthorizeUrl({state})` (scope `openid email profile`, `access_type=online`, `prompt=select_account`), `googleExchangeCode()` (client_secret_post token exchange), and `googleFetchProfile()` (OIDC userinfo, normalises `email_verified`). No secret/token is ever logged.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/api/auth/google/route.ts` (new) — GET start route: mints CSRF `state`, stashes it + validated `next` in a short-lived (600s) httpOnly/secure/sameSite=lax cookie scoped to `/api/auth/google`, 302s to Google. Bounces to `/login?error=google_unavailable` if creds are unset; IP rate-limited.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts` (new) — GET callback: handles Google's `error` param (declined / testing-mode) gracefully, verifies `state` vs cookie (CSRF), exchanges code, reads profile, **requires `email_verified`**. Find-or-link-or-create: by `googleId`, else by normalized email (links `googleId` onto the existing password account + stamps `emailVerifiedAt` if unset), else creates a new User with a random **unusable** bcrypt hash (since `passwordHash` is required/non-null), `emailVerifiedAt=now`, and a unique referral code matching `register()`. Writes audit rows, then issues the session and redirects to `/dashboard` (or `/admin`).
- `/opt/nxeon/app/login/page.tsx` — passes `googleEnabled={googleOauthConfigured()}` and maps `?error=` codes to friendly copy via a fixed allowlist (never echoes the raw query value).
- `/opt/nxeon/components/AuthForms.tsx` — added a "Continue with Google" button (inline four-colour Google glyph, Nxeon dark theme) with an "or" divider above the email/password form, wrapped in a `<div>`; the button is hidden entirely when `googleEnabled` is false.

### Session-issuance helper reused
`createSession(user.id)` from `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts` — the same helper `register()` and `login()` call. It signs the `nxeon_session` JWT (with `sub`, `sv` sessionVersion, `typ:"session"`), sets the httpOnly cookie with the admin-configurable expiry, and sets the JS-readable `nxeon_authed` flag. Called from the callback Route Handler so cookie writes land on the response; the callback is not a `"use server"` action, so no new server-action endpoint was introduced (guard test unaffected).

Notes: I did not run `db push`, build, deploy, or commit, per instructions. I also did not grant welcome credit / send the welcome email on Google signup (those helpers are private to `lib/actions.ts` and outside the scoped required-fields create); flag if you want parity there. Your memory notes mention keeping `DOCUMENTATION.md` current — I left docs untouched since the task was explicitly scoped.
